title: Shari'ah and fiqh
hook: shari'ah is the path Allah set; fiqh is the scholars' understanding of it

segments.voice: Yesterday closed the block on hadith, and your line: the chain held. Did you thank a living link, and what did they say? Day one thousand one hundred sixty-eight.

Two words get used as if they meant the same thing, in headlines and arguments and around dinner tables. Shari'ah. Fiqh. Inside the tradition they aren't the same, and the space between them is where this whole new block lives. One is the path Allah set. The other is the scholars' understanding of that path: written down, argued over, refined, sometimes corrected. A path, and maps of it drawn by careful people. A new block begins today, on fiqh and the schools of law, and it starts by telling the two apart. Today: shari'ah.
screen: `TWO WORDS, NOT ONE.` → `THE PATH.` → `AND THE MAPS OF IT.`

segments.voice: First, shari'ah. The word is in the Qur'an itself. In surah al-Jathiyah, Allah tells the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ that He has set him on a shari'ah, a clear road of the command, and tells him to follow it. So the word names something Allah sets, not something people invent. Second, fiqh. The word means understanding. In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet says that when Allah wants good for someone, He gives that person understanding of the religion, and the verb he uses there is the verb of fiqh. Fiqh is the scholars' work: reading the Qur'an and the sunnah closely and working out what they ask of a person in prayer, in fasting, in trade, in marriage, in the rest of a life. Third, why the difference matters. Muslims hold the shari'ah to come from Allah. Fiqh is human understanding of it, and a scholar can be right or wrong. Bukhari records the Prophet saying that a judge who strives to reach the right ruling and reaches it has two rewards, and one who strives and misses has one. An honest error, after real effort, is still rewarded. That's part of why there are schools of law, and why their differences can stand side by side. Fourth, the picture for this block. A map is drawn from the land by people who walked it carefully. Good maps can differ in what they show and how. None of them is the land itself. Sunni and Shia scholars both draw these maps, each with their own methods, and over the next days this block looks at the sources they draw from, beginning tomorrow with the Qur'an.
screen: `SHARI'AH: A ROAD ALLAH SETS.` · `FIQH: UNDERSTANDING.` · `TWO REWARDS, OR ONE.` · `THE MAP IS NOT THE LAND.`

segments.voice: The practice: learn the difference. Settle, and breathe. Say the two words slowly, one on each breath. Shari'ah: the path. Fiqh: the understanding, the map. Now take one ordinary act from your day: washing, eating, a piece of work, a kind word. Hold it, and ask two quiet questions. What is the path here, the good the act is aiming at? And what is the map, the detailed how-to that people have carefully worked out? Don't reach for answers. Just notice that there are two layers. Then let them rest, and breathe. The bell holds the time.
Shari'ah. The path Allah set, a word the Qur'an itself uses. Fiqh is the scholars' understanding of it. Today's word.

Your line: the path and the map. Today, when you hear the word shari'ah, ask whether the speaker means the path itself or someone's map of it. Tomorrow: the Qur'an as first source. Day one thousand one hundred sixty-eight.

howItsDone: Muslims who want to know how to pray, fast or trade rightly turn to fiqh, the rulings scholars have worked out, often through the books or teachers of one school of law.

fork.setup: you're a judge. you've studied the case and the texts with real care, and you're still not certain. what does the hadith in Bukhari say?
options: never rule until you're certain you're right.
strive and rule; an honest error after real effort still earns a reward.
fork.reveal: strive and get it right, two rewards; strive and miss, one. the effort is honored, which is part of why schools can differ with respect.

original.note: Arabic: a road, a way set out; the word the Qur'an uses in surah al-Jathiyah.

trapdoor: what you thought: shari'ah is a law code written down in one book.
what it means: shari'ah is the path Allah set; the written rulings are fiqh, the scholars' understanding of it.
what a scholar hears: shari'ah in surah al-Jathiyah, and fiqh as understanding, where a striving judge who misses still earns a reward.
